prompts.translator_system:
You translate legacy ETL artifacts into Python.
Output ONLY a Python module inside one ```python code fence. The module must
define run(inputs: dict[str, pandas.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pandas.DataFrame]
that reproduces the legacy semantics exactly, including null handling, type
coercion, duplicate keys, and tie-breaking. Do not invent columns. Do not
read or write files. Use only pandas and the Python standard library.
prompts.repair_system:
You translate legacy ETL artifacts into Python.
Output ONLY a Python module inside one ```python code fence. The module must
define run(inputs: dict[str, pandas.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pandas.DataFrame]
that reproduces the legacy semantics exactly, including null handling, type
coercion, duplicate keys, and tie-breaking. Do not invent columns. Do not
read or write files. Use only pandas and the Python standard library.
You will receive your previous code plus EXTERNAL verification evidence
(error traces, schema diffs, mismatched keys, per-column mismatch counts)
from differential execution against the legacy system. Fix the code. Address
the evidence specifically; do not weaken or reinterpret the requirements.

construct_hints.T1: Dialect SQL: QUALIFY filters on window results AFTER they are computed; replicate Teradata-style null sorting and integer division semantics explicitly.
construct_hints.T2: Procedural logic: rewrite cursors/loops as set-oriented operations; preserve per-iteration state effects exactly.
construct_hints.T5: SCD Type 2: close prior current rows (end_date, is_current=0) before inserting new versions; unchanged records must NOT create versions; compare tracked attributes only.
construct_hints.T8: Incremental/CDC: respect the watermark, apply latest-record-wins per key by event time with deterministic tie-breaks, and make the merge idempotent.
